findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with a renamed numbering part can exhaust the process stack
findings.summary: A document author can point the internal numbering relationship at deeply nested XML named `numbering.bin`. Admission skips XML depth and tag policy for that auxiliary filename, but the renderer parses it recursively, allowing a compact DOCX to terminate the conversion process.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document data deterministically bypasses the depth policy and can abort a local conversion or an embedding worker. Exposure is constrained to a caller choosing to process that document; no remote service or cross-tenant deployment is established, and SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits.
severity.changeConditions: A shared service accepting public document uploads without per-job process isolation would increase operational impact; enforcing XML limits at each semantic consumer removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects the extension-based admission decision, relationship-selected numbering part and unchecked recursive parser. No runtime trigger was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Render entry admits package
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-controlled DOCX bytes are admitted before the same bytes are normalized and opened.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses XML by extension
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml and .rels entries receive XML policy checks; a numbering.bin entry is treated as binary.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main part has an extension exception
codeEvidence.explanation: The extra check for non-XML names applies to the main document, leaving auxiliary relationship targets unchecked.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering relationship controls the selected part
codeEvidence.explanation: The document's internal numbering relationship selects an arbitrary package part, excluding external targets but imposing no XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Selected numbering bytes reach permissive parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected part is decoded as text and passed to the recursive DOM parser without checked parsing.

codeEvidence.label: DOM recursion has no depth argument
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recursively invokes parse_element; the skipped admission depth bound is the only protection on this path.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` classifies XML by filename and only adds a nonstandard-extension exception for the main part. `main_rel_part()` trusts internal relationship targets, so `load_numbering()` can select an auxiliary `.bin` part. `parse_numbering_xml()` invokes the permissive DOM parser, whose element recursion has no depth limit, without validating the selected bytes.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.

limitations: No malicious file was generated or executed.
Other XML consumers were not exhaustively enumerated; this finding establishes the numbering path.
validation.summary: Verified that `with_layout()` admits input, `admit()` omits XML checks on non-.xml/.rels auxiliary entries, `main_rel_part()` selects the attacker-controlled internal target, and `load_numbering()` parses it without a second check. PartFs inflation caps and strict translation constrain bytes but do not validate the auxiliary XML nesting.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admission extension filter -> internal numbering relationship -> part_string -> parse_numbering_xml -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled package relationship and auxiliary part bytes

impact.why: A stack overflow aborts the processing worker.

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to process attacker-provided DOCX; no public deployment is assumed.

limitations: Process isolation contains the failure to the selected job.

reachability.summary: Any caller processing a document supplied by a lower-trust author through the public render API can reach this path; neither external relationship fetching nor filesystem access is required.
reachability.entrypoint: convert::docx_to_pdf and the shared layout pipeline

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid DOCX whose numbering relationship targets a `.bin` entry containing deeply nested elements, then call `docx_to_pdf()` or another renderer using the shared layout pipeline.

remediationTests: Render a DOCX with a deeply nested `numbering.bin` relationship target and assert an INVALID_XML refusal before DOM construction.
Retain support for nonstandard auxiliary filenames within the configured XML limits.

findings.title: Importing a cyclic drawing payload can terminate Markdown conversion
findings.summary: A Markdown author can supply a `drawing:` image payload with a dependency that points to itself. JSON decoding accepts that graph and package assembly recursively materializes it without tracking visited dependencies, exhausting the conversion process stack.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-supplied Markdown image payload can abort a caller processing it, including native or WASM conversion. This is a constrained document-processing availability failure; remote multi-user deployment is not established and process quotas are a caller obligation.
severity.changeConditions: A shared unisolated Markdown conversion service would increase impact; rejecting cycles or memoizing in-progress parts removes the deterministic trigger.

confidence.rationale: Independent source trace verifies direct public Markdown acceptance, unvalidated dependency indices, and recursive traversal with no cycle guard; no application code was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Public Markdown conversion
codeEvidence.explanation: The public API accepts the caller's Markdown, including drawing destinations.

codeEvidence.label: Drawing destination decoded without graph validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Base64 JSON becomes Drawing with caller-selected dependency indices; deserialization supplies no graph traversal control.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded drawing enters the output model
codeEvidence.explanation: The writer accepts a drawing URL and stores the decoded structure for package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Package assembly walks root dependencies
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal relationship with a valid dependency index invokes dep_part.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency traversal recurses before recording a completed part
codeEvidence.explanation: The function records only chosen output names and recursively follows valid inner indices without visited or in-progress graph state.

codeEvidence.label: Package emitter calls materialize
codeEvidence.explanation: Package emission passes the attacker-supplied Drawing to the recursive materializer.

rootCause.summary: `picture()` accepts a decoded `Drawing` from caller-controlled Markdown and package assembly invokes `materialize()`. Root relationships select dependency indices. `dep_part()` inserts a generated filename into `used`, but does not mark the dependency index as in progress or completed before following its relationships. A self-edge therefore re-enters the same dependency indefinitely; filename collision handling does not stop the graph recursion.

findings.remediation: Validate and bound the drawing dependency graph before assembly; use a per-index in-progress/completed map to reject cycles or allocate each output part once before resolving links.

limitations: No crafted input was generated or executed.
A valid captured graph cycle may also reproduce this, but the proven path is author-supplied Markdown.
validation.summary: Verified a single dependency with `rels[].part` pointing to its own valid index passes the only index checks. `dep_part()` recursively invokes itself before writing/comparing the part bytes. Capture-time MAX_DEPS and JSON nesting limits do not constrain this flat cyclic graph, and no graph validation is performed by decode().

dataflow.summary: caller Markdown -> picture -> drawing::decode -> document.drawings -> package::drawing -> materialize -> recursive dep_part
dataflow.outcome: stack exhaustion and process or WASM-instance termination

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to import the attacker's Markdown; no public service is assumed.

reachability.summary: Any consumer of the public Markdown-to-DOCX API that converts a document from a lower-trust author can trigger the path with default options; no local file or network access is required.

attackPath.summary: Pass Markdown containing a `drawing:` image URL whose decoded root relationship points to dependency 0 and whose dependency 0 relationship points back to 0 to `markdown_to_docx()`.

remediationTests: Import a self-referential dependency and a two-node cycle and assert bounded refusal or safe graph-preserving completion.
Import a shared acyclic dependency graph and assert each part is emitted once.

surfaces.label: Release, CI and automated review privilege boundaries
surfaces.riskArea: CI trust and shared build cache
surfaces.notes: Focused reviewer found no ordinary contributor-to-release secret or direct shell-injection path. release.yml:15-21 is tag-only; release job owns contents:write at :230-265; artifact downloads are own-run at :230-250; signing temp keys cleaned at :261-309. scripts/release.sh:230-289 constrains version and :552-648 quotes summaries; eval at :1092-1100 receives fixed call strings. Jules workflows transfer metadata through env and reject fork heads before checkout (.github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:33-110,214-324; jules-review.yml:18-40). However PR CI executes repository/local-action code on self-hosted runners (.github/workflows/ci.yml:14-48,72-101,252-310; docs.yml:42-99; adoption.yml:16-31,48-102; md-roundtrip.yml:13-39). mbx action configures http://mbx-cache:7543 namespace jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines without a credential (.github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-26,33-52), while comments claim protected-push-only publication. Actual server authorization, cache object integrity, network isolation, fork approval and ephemeral runner controls are absent and unresolved; client read mode does not prove server authorization. No confirmed poisoning/credential disclosure.

threatModel.summary: Jubarte processes untrusted DOCX/OOXML, Markdown, and legacy DOC into document views, edited packages, tracked-change redlines, PDF/PNG, and reports. The Rust engine is consumed by its native CLI, PyO3 Python APIs/CLI, and wasm-bindgen browser/Node APIs and Node CLI. Python additionally provides a stdio MCP server with explicit directory-capability document/artifact I/O. Native rendering also performs ambient font discovery and font-index persistence, so the engine is not universally filesystem-pure. The optional native self-update command downloads a GitHub release and replaces the executable; release automation separately holds publication/signing authority. Sources: src/lib.rs:7-35, src/lib.rs:163-165, Cargo.toml:82-99, jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:31-39, jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:14-32, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, src/convert/font.rs:3090-3107, src/convert/font.rs:3213-3229, src/update.rs:186-257, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-265.
assets: Confidential document content, embedded media, revisions, comments, authors, metadata, rendered output, and edit reports entrusted to the processing host and intentionally returned or exported by its selected interface. These are not encrypted by the engine. Sources: src/lib.rs:17-30, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217, SECURITY.md:79-85.

Integrity of document edits and correspondence between a plan and its intended input snapshot. The legacy edit path verifies source_sha256 when provided; this guard is optional and recorded as guarded in its report. Sources: src/edit.rs:2081-2088, src/edit.rs:2480-2482.

Filesystem authority granted to MCP: canonical root and paths beneath it, including out_dir/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json, optional redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png; render exports use out_dir/page-NN.png and render.pdf. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108,185-217,234-255.

Host filesystem integrity outside intentionally authorized CLI destinations and Markdown image resource roots. Native CLI publication uses ambient destination-parent authority; MCP uses a held root capability. Sources: src/publication.rs:146-165,175-225, src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273,2858-2871.

Native renderer fonts and persistent index. Defaults: macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv; Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv; Windows $APPDATA\jubarte\font-index.tsv. Environment overrides change locations. Sources: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229.

Embedding-process availability and CPU/memory. Default admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per-part and 256 MiB total inflated; compare permits 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated. Both retain 10,000 entries and XML depth 256. Sources: src/admission.rs:63-99.

Installed executable integrity and release credentials. Current updater trusts GitHub transport plus SHA256SUMS.txt, with no compiled signing key/threshold. Release signing uses ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY reference; GitHub uses GITHUB_TOKEN, local release also uses registry credentials. Sources: src/update.rs:25-48,198-257, .github/workflows/release.yml:261-309,356-369, scripts/release.sh:370-380,919-959,1069.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document bytes -> in-process ZIP/OPC/XML/rendering. Admission precedes representative public parsing paths and applies active resource/XML limits. Inspection uses defaults; PDF/PNG layout uses admit_package and compare limits. Checked XML validates before DOM; infallible parse_xdocument deliberately does not. Sources: src/admission.rs:13-28, src/inspect.rs:604-622, src/convert/mod.rs:768-778, src/document_comparer.rs:4922-4928, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:84-135.

ZIP central/local records -> shared production opener. open_archive runs zip_defects before returning; unchecked opening is distinct diagnostic/admission machinery. Sources: src/opc/archive.rs:15-20,34-51.

Stdio MCP client -> filesystem host. --root defaults to cwd, is expanded/canonicalized, native _OutputRoot opens once. Python containment is diagnostic; actual reads/writes use held capability. Outputs additionally validate portable relative names, refuse symlinks, use atomic hard-link no-clobber without overwrite. Tool annotations are hints, not separate caller authorization. Sources: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381, jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278, src/publication.rs:146-199,228-254,448-463,558-570.

Native CLI operator -> ambient input/output paths. std::fs::read inputs and publish_paths holds selected destination parents, stages .jubarte-<uuid>.partial/bytes. Atomic per file, not whole set. Distinct from MCP root confinement. Sources: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2742,261-273, src/publication.rs:168-173,203-225,418-482.

Python/Node CLI operators -> ambient files. Python Path.read_bytes/write_bytes and Node fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync are independent I/O.
